what makes a sentence a run on

A run-on welds two complete sentences together with nothing strong enough between them: I missed the bus I walked. The comma splice is its sibling: I missed the bus, I walked ✍️ You have four repairs — full stop, semicolon, a joining word like so, or a comma plus that word. Length is not the fault; a long sentence can be perfectly built. Repair mine your way.[CHIPS]So I walked|Semicolon version|Long correct example[/CHIPS]

why can a pie chart be misleading

A pie asks your eye to compare angles, which eyes are genuinely bad at — a 22% slice and a 25% slice are very hard to tell apart in a circle 🥧. Tilt it into 3D and the near slices swell for free. Worst of all, a pie insists the parts add to one whole, so any survey where people ticked several answers breaks it. A plain bar chart usually reads truer 📊. [CHIPS]When pies work|Bar chart instead|Test my eye[/CHIPS]

how do lizards walk up the walls in my house

how did dogs come from wolves

Same mechanism as natural selection, but with humans doing the choosing. 🐕 Wolves that tolerated people got scraps and bred nearby; humans then picked the calmest, later the best herders, later the ones with the right ears. Because we selected hard for specific traits every generation, change came fast — thousands of years, not millions. A pug still shares ancestry you can read in its DNA. [CHIPS]What artificial selection is|Why breeds have problems[/CHIPS]

why is the loudspeaker from the next street clearer at night

why can't i see colours properly in a dark room

Your retina carries two kinds of sensor. Cones read colour but need a decent amount of light; rods are far more sensitive yet report no colour at all.
